items.stem: You must rename a heavily used column without downtime. What approach is safest?

options.text: Expand (add the new column), migrate (backfill and dual-write), then contract (drop the old column)
options.rationale: Correct: the expand-migrate-contract pattern keeps old and new readers working throughout.

options.text: Run a single ALTER TABLE RENAME during peak traffic
options.rationale: A direct rename can break current readers and may lock the table.

options.text: Drop the old column first, then add the new one
options.rationale: Dropping first loses data and breaks existing queries immediately.

options.text: Ask the AI tool to rename it and deploy without review
options.rationale: Unreviewed migrations on live tables are high-risk.

items.explanation: Correct: the expand-migrate-contract pattern keeps old and new readers working throughout.

items.stem: An AI tool drafted a backfill migration. Which TWO things must you verify before running it in production? (Select TWO.)

options.text: That it runs in batches and avoids long-held locks on large tables
options.rationale: Correct: unbatched backfills can lock tables and cause outages.

options.text: That it is backward-compatible with code still reading the old shape
options.rationale: Correct: readers on the old schema must keep working during rollout.

options.text: That the script is written in the newest SQL dialect
options.rationale: Dialect novelty is irrelevant to safety.

options.text: That the AI used the most tokens available
options.rationale: Token usage says nothing about migration correctness or safety.

items.explanation: Correct: unbatched backfills can lock tables and cause outages.

items.stem: A migration completed with no errors. Why is that not sufficient evidence of success?

options.text: No error does not prove the data was transformed and preserved correctly; validation is still required
options.rationale: Correct: correctness must be verified with counts, checksums and spot checks.

options.text: Migrations that run without errors are always correct
options.rationale: Absence of errors does not guarantee correct data transformation.

options.text: Error-free means rollback is never needed
options.rationale: A silent data error can still require rollback.

options.text: It means the schema no longer needs backups
options.rationale: Backups remain essential regardless of migration outcome.

items.explanation: Correct: correctness must be verified with counts, checksums and spot checks.
